paper_metadata.title: Effect of boron on microstructure evolution and hot tensile deformation behavior of Ti-5Al-5V-5Mo-1Cr-1Fe alloy

evidence.quote: Ti-5Al-5V-5Mo-1Cr-1Fe (Ti-55511), one of the near β-Ti alloys is considered to be the candidate material for high strength applications.

In the bare alloy, primary α-phase with an elongated morphology in transformed β matrix is observed.
The α-phase has become finer and globular in an equiaxed grain structure of the matrix upon addition of 0.06% B.
However, further increase in B to 0.12% led to slight coarsening of α-phase.

Elongated α phase along the tensile axis can also be observed along with boride whiskers of ~4 µm width and 20-30 µm length with bright contrast in optical micrographs (Fig. 9b, c) and dark contrast in SEM micrograph (Fig. 9d).

The cavitation (indicated with dotted circles) at the boride-matrix interface or decohesion/ cracking of borides in the matrix was higher in 0.12% B containing alloy compared to that in the Ti-55511-0.06B alloy deformed under the same conditions.
The bare alloy failed prematurely due to the presence of coarse and elongated lamellar α phase in β-matrix.
The near β-Ti alloy, Ti-5Al-5V-5Mo-1Cr-1Fe has undergone significant grain refinement and globularization of α-phase upon addition of 0.06 wt.% of boron.
However, further increase in boron to 0.12% has led to coarsening and agglomeration of α-phase and increased volume fraction of boride whiskers.

Ti-55511-0.12B alloy failed prematurely compared to the Ti-55511-0.06B alloy due to cavitation occurring at the boride particle-matrix interface.
The alloy exhibits high yield strength (σy~1100 MPa) and ultimate tensile strength (σTS~1250 MPa) and limited elongation to failure (ef~8%) in solution treated and aged (STA) condition [4].
